Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn K2-Play Completes Final Phase of North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan Oct 15, 2026 FRUITA, Colo. – Over the past eight years, the North Fruita Desert has changed in ways riders can see as soon as they arrive. There are more miles of singletrack, more places to camp and dedicated space for races and other large events, all part of a broader effort by the Bureau of Land Management and community partners to keep pace with one of western Colorado’s busiest recreation areas. This fall, the final trail in the North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan is complete. K2-Play winds for about three miles along the base of the Book Cliffs and completes the final phase of a roughly 30-mile expansion of the 18 Road trail system. Its completion caps years of planning and construction involving the BLM Grand Junction Field Office, Colorado Plateau Mountain Bike Trail Association, Mesa County, City of Fruita, local businesses, professional trail builders and volunteers. pages.text: Learn about the United States' founding documents | USAGov Skip to main content Learn about the United States' founding documents The Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, and Bill of Rights, known together as the Charters of Freedom, established the government’s structure and continue to secure the rights of American citizens. Declaration of Independence The Declaration of Independence proclaimed that the American colonies were separating from British rule, and detailed the reasons. On July 4, 1776, Congress voted to accept the Declaration of Independence, marking July 4 as Independence Day. Thomas Jefferson, the principal author, drafted the document in 17 days. U.S. Constitution The Constitution of the United States set up the foundation of the U.S. government, including its purpose and structure. The Constitutional Convention adopted the Constitution on September 17, 1787. Bill of Rights The Bill of Rights is the first 10 amendments (changes) to the U.S. Constitution. It guarantees greater protection for individual freedoms and lists specific limits on government power. The Constitution has 27 amendments in all. Last updated on 8 November 2026. Ten years ago, I attended my first State of the Map LATAM in São Paulo, thanks to a travel grant. Until then, for me, OpenStreetMap was just the group we’d formed in Mexico out of the legendary Rancho Electrónico, Mexico City’s hackerspace. During those days, I discovered it was so much more: a regional community, with faces, stories, perspectives, and generosity. I understood why these in-person gatherings matter so much. They gave rise to friendships that have lasted a decade—sometimes in person and mostly online—and I believe that through these networks we’ve accomplished important things. From that very first time, together with other women, we also decided to promote inclusion and diversity in the community, and that’s how Geochicas was born. That’s why, when I decided to lead the Mexican edition, I did so with great enthusiasm. It was a whole year of intense emotions, thinking about bringing well-known figures and new people from across the region to my city, happy at the idea that they would experience the city at its best and, hopefully, learn more about its cultural details.
